newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end higher in all months.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end higher in all months.

text.p: The yen-based gold futures market ended higher across the board on Tuesday, as firmer bullion prices offset the yen's gains against the dollar, traders said.
The most-active benchmark October 1997 contract finished six yen per gram higher at 1,353 yen. Other prices were two to nine yen per gram lower.

The prices were mixed in early morning trade, as local investors could not find clear direction, traders said. Buying emerged later, however, as firmer bullion prices encouraged individual investors, they said.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $381.65/382.15 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $381.50/90 in New York on Monday.
Yen-based platinum futures ended higher across the board, in line with gold. Prices were eight to 15 yen per gram higher, with the benchmark October 1997 contract up 14 yen at 1,382.

Some traders cited a news on Tuesday that the Russian platinum group metal agency would delay sending a delegation to Japan to negotiate its annual export contract for 1997 until January or February as a bullish factor.
Yen-based palladium futures ended mixed, with prices ranging from two yen per gram lower to two yen higher. The benchmark October contract was down one yen at 422 yen.
Yen-based silver futures were mixed at the closing. The benchmark October was up 1.3 yen at 178.5. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7391
